scope: Conditional thermal envelope and complete required-state coverage audit. No assembly temperature, physical result, or qualified circuit is claimed. Null means unknown; no reference data is substituted for it.
heat_accounting: Every composed-netlist component and harness segment has one heat owner. U4 and Sparkle use local conversion/internal losses, excluding forwarded output power counted at loads. Cell heat includes electrochemical effects; capacitor heat includes ESR and release. Optical escape, radio emission and cooling credit are zero unless independently bounded. New or hidden physical paths still require the complete-circuit premise. Combined owners need separate member temperature limits and transfer bounds covering every possible internal heat distribution. LED transfer bounds must also cover every possible optical reabsorption site; depositing all photon energy at the LED junction alone does not bound other surfaces.
model_conditions: A fixed passive linear thermal network, or a proved dominating one, with nonnegative impulse responses and bounded boundary and ALL internal initial temperature intervals. Transfer coefficients include cross heating/cooling, material/contact/airflow/wearing uncertainty. Signed local power must remain between -cooling_upper_w and heat_upper_w instantaneously over the whole temperature range, including repeated events. Zero cooling needs evidence; it is not inferred from an upper heat bound. Averaged PWM or short pulses need a separately qualified transient model.

efuse_operating_range.sections: Features and description: characterized operating junction range -40 C to +125 C

thermal_metrics.sections: 1 and 1.1, PDF p. 2: package RthetaJA depends on test board and boundary conditions

efuse.facts: 125 C recommended junction maximum. 41.7 and 74.5 K/W are simulations on different four-layer test PCBs, not enclosure bounds. 45 mOhm maximum at 3 A is not a linear-mode loss model. Thermal shutdown does not qualify cell or touch temperature.

boost.sections: Typical efficiencies and maximum output currents
boost.facts: Efficiency and current plots are typical; achieved current depends on ambient, airflow and heat sinking. The 85% reference is not a guaranteed efficiency minimum.

states.normal: Continuous operation; bound every local heat source over the operating voltage and temperature range.
states.pwm_radio_peak: Coincident LED PWM and radio peaks; average brightness is not an instantaneous heat bound.
states.startup: Capacitor charge, boost inrush and eFuse linear operation through KILL blanking; no I-squared-R assumption in current limit.
states.absent_cell: OFF and ON with cell absent, including retained B/C/output charge and signal ingress.
states.depleted_cell: Hardware cutoff with S1 still ON; controller, bleeders and other residual dissipation remain.
states.reversed_cell: Both switch positions and retained positive rails; include all power/control pin injection and contact heat.
states.contact_bounce: Intermittent contacts while ON and during insertion; include arcing and accumulated heating.
states.voltage_rebound: Voltage recovery after depletion; no idealized reset or automatic cooling credit.
states.rapid_replacement: Warm initial assembly and charged rails before qualified discharge; bound repeated inrush.
states.charged_capacitors: Stored-energy discharge in all rails including USB-isolated and backpowered states.
states.overload: Continuous and transient overload including eFuse linear dissipation and thermal latch-off.
states.short: F1 backup, prefuse and load faults; peak heat and capacitor release require separate current/energy evidence.
states.cleared_fault: Warm restart after fault removal; electronics reset does not reset temperature or repair a blown fuse.
states.usb_service: Cell removed and USB 5 V; bound signal/backfeed losses and USB power independently of the battery protector.

remaining_evidence: Lower boundary and initial temperature bounds, minimum operating temperatures for every observer, and instantaneous cooling magnitudes for all sources. Unknown signed cell heat cannot be treated as zero cooling; hot-limit success cannot certify cold operation.
Complete circuit waveforms for every state, all pin and source conditions, repeated transitions and stored-energy release. Existing partial DC/reset/fault models do not supply these.

Instantaneous local heat bounds for all owned parts and conductors, including cell electrochemistry, converter losses, capacitor ESR, controller and bleeders; source conditions must cover the resulting temperature range.

Separate enclosure transfer coefficients for both designs, including PCB copper, print/material/contact tolerances, optics, clothing/skin contact, ambient and solar heat; no datasheet test-board substitution.
Bound initial stored heat through swaps/fault recovery, all environmental temperatures and sustained external heating. A source-free OFF interval is not a thermal reset.
Component, cell, insulation and front/rear surface operating limits with source/conditions. The 125 C eFuse limit does not establish safe touching or wearing.
